record_type_quote:
A previous study found that task shifting and fluid intelligence, but not working memory

capacity (WMC) and prior knowledge, influenced the worked example effect (Schwaighofer,

Bühner, & Fischer, 2016). To increase confidence in these findings, we report a pre-

registered extended replication study of Schwaighofer et al.’s investigation.

targets.authors: Schwaighofer, M., Bühner, M., & Fischer, F.
targets.title: Executive functions as moderators of the worked example effect: When shifting is more important than working memory capacity.
targets.evidence_quote:
A previous study found that task shifting and fluid intelligence, but not working memory

capacity (WMC) and prior knowledge, influenced the worked example effect (Schwaighofer,

Bühner, & Fischer, 2016). To increase confidence in these findings, we report a pre-

registered extended replication study of Schwaighofer et al.’s investigation.
targets.outcome_quote:
Results showed that the advantage of worked examples

over problem-solving decreased with increasing prior knowledge, suggesting that problem-

solving becomes eventually more effective than worked example study. Similarly, the benefit

of worked examples over problem-solving decreased with increasing shifting ability of a

learner. However, contingencies on WMC or fluid intelligence were not detected.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original shifting moderation and WMC null repeated; original fluid-intelligence moderation was absent, and prior-knowledge moderation appeared in contrast to the original. Discussion explicitly identifies these contrasts, with no overriding overall success verdict.

reasoning: Matching title, DOI printed on cover, and all six authors verify the full accepted manuscript. One original 2016 paper is targeted; related 2017 papers are not targets.
